summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) is in a tense pause with limited incidents: the US carried out what it called limited defensive strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran is still attacking ships around the strait, and the US blockade of Iranian ports continues while indirect talks go on. Hormuz is open only in part, with oil flows well below normal.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are open under US control. Most ships now pass through a US-run transit system (101 transits over Oct 22–24, against about 138 a day in 2025), with only a handful a day outside it.

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: Around 11.6 to 11.7 million barrels a day in October, against about 17.1 million before the war (Kpler).

status.label: The war
status.note: The US carried out 'limited defensive' strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz after surface-to-air missile threats against US assets (AP, via Al Jazeera, Nov 3); the Wall Street Journal, citing US officials, reported a strike on Qeshm Island as one of a series of limited strikes in recent weeks (via Gulf News). Indirect talks continue; Vice President Vance said there has been progress.

status.label: Brent crude
status.note: Trading Economics showed Brent near US$104.08 late Tuesday morning, down about 0.7% on the day, after it fell below US$102 earlier in the session; WTI was near US$96.29. Brent settled at US$104.77 on Monday, down 7.6%.

updates.text: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the overnight attacks on Iran's Qeshm Island had not affected oil flows (Trading Economics market report).

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei had given the government 'certain authorities' over talks with the US and that Tehran would seek to resolve the conflict through dialogue; Qatari mediators travelled to Tehran on Monday night (Al Jazeera).

Iran's chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf said Iran had delivered a 'firm and rational response' to the US and that the ball was in America's court; Iran says it has a two-day plan to reopen the strait and resume nuclear talks if Washington meets its demands, including lifting the blockade (AP).

An India-flagged vessel with 14 Indian seafarers aboard was struck by an unidentified aerial object off Oman; one Indian crew member died and 13 were rescued (CBS News live updates). Who launched it was not stated.
Oil edged higher in early Asian trade after Monday's plunge: Brent was up 0.5% at US$105.25 at 01:04 GMT, after reports of the US strike on Qeshm Island (Reuters).
Trump said the US would not launch new attacks before Tuesday's midterm elections, without ruling out later action.

Iranian negotiators left Doha without a breakthrough; messages continue through Qatari mediators, and an official briefed on the talks told Reuters a draft proposal is circulating. No agreement on reopening the strait has been announced.

The US military carried out limited defensive strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz after surface-to-air missile threats against US assets (AP); the Wall Street Journal, citing US officials, reported a strike on Qeshm Island, the strait's largest island. Vice President JD Vance said the US has made progress in indirect talks; Iran says the US must first lift its naval blockade.
sources: Al Jazeera live (citing AP): US carries out defensive strikes in Strait of Hormuz
Gulf News: US carries out defensive strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
